as_written_in_papers.quote: In family 3, the c.1412G>C p.(Arg471Pro) in NOD2 was found in the heterozygous state in all five family members
In family 3, two variants of unknown significance in a heterozygous state were found: c.1412G>T p.(Arg471Leu) in NOD2 and c.928C>T p.(Arg310*) in NLRC4 (NM_001199139.1).
NM_022162.3 was taken as the reference sequence.

cases.statement: Five heterozygous carriers in one three-generation family (family 3): triplet sisters III:1 (proband), III:2 (monozygotic with III:1) and III:3 (dizygotic), their mother II:1 and maternal grandfather I:1. All five have camptodactyly; uveitis is present in III:1, III:2 and II:1.

people.label: III:1
people.other_allele: not applicable (autosomal dominant); also carries NLRC4 c.928C>T p.(Arg310*)
people.key_phenotypes: panuveitis from 12 years with conjunctival granulomas and corneal opacities; camptodactyly of fourth fingers; flexion deformities of elbows and ankles; preschool generalized rash; probable polyarthritis

quotes.quote: The proband from family 3 (III:1, Figure 1) was referred at 12 years old with a one-year history of panuveitis.
Conjunctival granulomas, corneal opacities, posterior synechiae and a few chorioretinal, atrophic, partially pigmented circular lesions in the periphery were found (Figure 4A–C).
She had flexion deformities in the elbows and ankles and camptodactyly of the fourth finger bilaterally (Figures S2A and S3A).

At preschool age, she suffered from a non-itching generalized severe skin rash treated as atopic dermatitis, which completely resolved upon topical corticosteroid treatment within 2 years, and no skin problems occurred thereafter.

people.label: III:2
people.other_allele: not applicable (autosomal dominant); also carries NLRC4 c.928C>T p.(Arg310*)
people.key_phenotypes: ankle tenosynovitis from 6 years; camptodactyly of fingers 3-4 and toe 5; mild preschool rash; conjunctival granulomas, corneal opacities and asymptomatic posterior uveitis; congenital pes equinovarus

quotes.quote: The monozygotic triplet sister (III:2, Figure 1) had joint problems from 6 years of age, when she developed tenosynovitis in both ankles, which was originally diagnosed as JIA.
She also had camptodactyly in fingers three and four bilaterally as well as toe five (Figures S2B and S3B).
In her preschool years, she had a mild skin rash on the trunk and extremities that did not itch and resolved after topical corticosteroids.

Ophthalmic examination revealed conjunctival granulomas, corneal opacities and asymptomatic posterior uveitis characterized by a few chorioretinal, partially pigmented lesions in the periphery, predominantly in the inferior region.

people.label: III:3
people.key_phenotypes: camptodactyly of fingers 4-5 only; no joint problems; no uveitis

quotes.quote: The dizygotic triplet sister (Figure 1, individual III:3), examined for the first time when aged 10 years and 17 years at the last follow-up visit, had no joint problems or uveitis.
She had camptodactyly of fingers four and five (Figure S2C).

people.label: II:1 (Family 3)
people.other_allele: not applicable (autosomal dominant); also carries NLRC4 c.928C>T p.(Arg310*) and two ABCC6 variants in trans (PXE)
people.key_phenotypes: bilateral inactive posterior uveitis; camptodactyly of fingers 3-5; no arthritis; angioid streaks and neck papules attributed to PXE

quotes.quote: The mother of the triplet sisters (Figure 1, individual II:1), examined at 43 years, had bilateral signs of inactive posterior uveitis with peripheral, chorioretinal, partially pigmented lesions and optic nerve drusen (Figure 4D–F).
She also had marked camptodactyly of fingers 3–5 (Figure S2D) but never suffered from arthritis.
She denied the presence of skin rush in childhood.

people.label: I:1
people.key_phenotypes: mild camptodactyly of fingers 4-5 only; no skin or joint problems; no uveitis

quotes.quote: The 66 year-old grandfather of the proband from family 3 (I:1; Figure 1) never reported skin or joint problems, though he has been treated for type 2 diabetes mellitus.
He had mild camptodactyly of fingers four and five (Figure S2E).
There were no signs of uveitis upon ocular examination.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Only III:1 has the full triad; others have partial features (uveitis, tenosynovitis, camptodactyly). Other causes were searched: an 89-gene autoimmune/autoinflammatory panel in III:1 and III:2 found an additional NLRC4 variant; exome sequencing in II:1 found two ABCC6 variants in trans explaining PXE features and no other rare variants in camptodactyly genes. The authors note camptodactyly could be an independent trait.

quotes.quote: In the proband from family 3 (individual III:1, Figure 1) and their sister (III:2, Figure 1), targeted next-generation sequencing using an autoimmune panel containing 89 genes was performed (Supplementary Materials).
Except for c.1412G>C in NOD2, another heterozygous variant classified as a VUS was identified: c.928C>T p.(Arg310*) in NLRC4 (NM_001199139.1).
Subsequent segregation analysis (Figure 1) confirmed their trans configuration.
No other rare, possibly pathogenic variants in genes associated with camptodactyly were identified.
We also considered that camptodactyly could be an independent trait or sign of a different disease [10,41].

segregation.statement: Five carriers across three generations, all with camptodactyly; uveitis in three (III:1, III:2, II:1), arthritis or tenosynovitis in two (III:1, III:2), camptodactyly only in two (III:3, I:1). Unaffected non-carriers are not described. The co-segregating NLRC4 variant came from the maternal grandmother, described as unaffected; uveitis occurred only in members carrying both variants. III:1 and III:2 are monozygotic.

quotes.quote: In family 3, the c.1412G>C p.(Arg471Pro) in NOD2 was found in the heterozygous state in all five family members (Figure 1), of which only one had a classical triad of BS including uveitis, and two had uveitis, one of whom had documented skin rush, while two exhibited camptodactyly only.
All five heterozygous carriers of c.1412G>C in NOD2 had camptodactyly.
Interestingly, uveitis was only present in members who also harbored c.928C>T in NLRC4.
Segregation analysis showed that this change was inherited from an unaffected maternal grandmother and hence unlikely to be disease-causing (Figure 1).
Sanger sequencing was used for segregation analysis within the families.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo in the triplets or their mother: the variant is present in the mother (II:1) and the maternal grandfather (I:1). Whether it arose de novo in I:1 is not reported.

quotes.quote: In family 3, the c.1412G>C p.(Arg471Pro) in NOD2 was found in the heterozygous state in all five family members

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense (Arg444Pro on NP_001357395.1; stated as p.(Arg471Pro) on NM_022162.3; the abstract instead says c.1412G>T p.(Arg471Leu)). The authors state the presumed mechanism of Blau-causing changes in general terms.

quotes.quote: The presumed mechanism of BS-causing mutations is faulty canonical signaling and reduced IRF4-mediated cross-regulation [37].

computational_predictions.statement: As reported: REVEL 0.14, which the authors place in their lower (moderately non-damaging) range.

quotes.quote: However, the meta-predictor REVEL score for this variant was 0.14 (i.e., in the range of moderately benign).

population_data_in_papers.statement: Not present in gnomAD v.4.0.0; not reported in the literature per the authors.

quotes.quote: This variant has not been reported in the literature, and it is not present in the gnomAD v.4.0.0 dataset.

authors_classification.statement: Authors classify c.1412G>C as a VUS under ACMG-AMP (Franklin platform) and say more carriers are needed to prove causality.

quotes.quote: Based on the ACMG-AMP criteria, the c.1412G>C in NOD2 was classified as a VUS.
The limitation of the current study is that to prove the causality of c.1412G>C in NOD2, more BS patients carrying the same variant need to be identified.

concerns: The paper contradicts itself: the abstract gives c.1412G>T p.(Arg471Leu), the results and discussion give c.1412G>C p.(Arg471Pro). The batch follows the c.1412G>C form.
Numbering: the paper uses NM_022162.3; the batch's NM_001370466.1 numbers are 81 nt / 27 codons lower (c.1412 -> c.1331; R471 -> R444).
Second candidate variant: NLRC4 c.928C>T p.(Arg310*) in III:1, III:2 and II:1 (from the maternal grandmother); uveitis occurs only in carriers of both variants.
II:1 also has two ABCC6 variants in trans (PXE), which explain her angioid streaks and neck papules.
III:1 and III:2 are monozygotic triplets, so they are not independent observations.
NOD2 testing in the probands covered exon 4 by Sanger; panel testing was done only in III:1 and III:2, exome only in II:1.

Camptodactyly, the one feature shared by all carriers, is considered by the authors as possibly an independent trait; three carriers also had hallux valgus surgery, which the authors judge coincidental.
notes_for_panel: One family (PMID 38927735) with five heterozygous carriers and variable expression; the authors themselves leave the variant unresolved and raise a possible contribution from a co-segregating NLRC4 nonsense variant.
